stages.name: Exploitation of Perimeter and Developer Tools
observables: HTTP POST to /forgot-password in Flowise
Unauthenticated CI lint API calls to GitLab
PHP file uploads to /wp-content/plugins/bug-library/
Command injection patterns in Citrix NetScaler login logs
SQL injection patterns in Cisco Secure Email Gateway S/MIME handling

stages.name: NTLMv2 Hash Disclosure via UNC Path
observables: OpenBullet2 forced SMB authentication via UNC path proxy source
Outbound SMB (port 445) connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure

stages.name: Multi-Protocol Fetch Payload Execution
observables: Fetch commands using FTP, HTTP, HTTPS, or TFTP to download LoongArch64 payloads
Execution of chmod on downloaded files
Reverse shell or bind shell activity (e.g., shell_reverse_tcp)

stages.name: Linux ELF Executable Payload Injection
observables: Code cave and segment injection in Linux ELF files
Architecture-specific trampolines for x86, x64, or AArch64
Modified ELF binaries on disk

stages.name: Docker Container Persistence and Host Access
observables: Creation of privileged Docker containers
Bind-mounting host filesystem (e.g., C: drive on Windows or root on Linux) to a container
Docker Desktop creating persistent Alpine containers on Windows
Portainer API activity to create containers with host access

scenario.summary: This campaign involves the use of newly released Metasploit modules targeting unauthenticated RCE and authentication bypass vulnerabilities in perimeter devices and developer tools like Citrix NetScaler, Cisco Secure Email Gateway, Flowise, and GitLab. After initial access, attackers leverage specialized Linux ELF injection techniques and privileged Docker container creation for persistent access and payload execution.

meta.rationale: Focus on Linux servers, Docker hosts, and systems with direct internet egress. Use the scope_hosts parameter if focusing on specific segments containing perimeter appliances.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder is staging non-standard architecture payloads using multi-protocol fetch adapters and establishing persistence via Linux ELF binary injection or privileged Docker containers with host root mounts.

hunt.name: Advanced Persistence and Payload Staging
hunt.description: This hunt examines tradecraft associated with recent Metasploit releases, focusing on post-exploitation staging and persistence. It targets the delivery of LoongArch64 payloads via FTP, TFTP, and HTTP, the modification of system-critical ELF binaries on Linux, and the use of Docker containers to mount host filesystems for high-privilege persistence. The hunt uses a gated flow, starting with a cheap lead query for suspicious process behavior before opening detailed network and file-level audits for corroboration.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, current_directory, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%loongarch64%' OR (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%chmod%' AND (instr(process_cmd_line, ' +x') > 0 OR instr(process_cmd_line, ' 777') > 0)) OR (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%docker%' AND (instr(process_cmd_line, '--privileged') > 0 OR instr(process_cmd_line, '-v /') > 0))) AND ('{{suspicious_paths}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{suspicious_paths}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(current_directory) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify initial signs of payload staging, rare architecture references, or dangerous Docker configurations in process command lines.
config.expected_signal: Process rows showing chmod commands in temporary directories, mentions of LoongArch64, or Docker commands with host filesystem mounts. Silence proves no common CLI staging patterns occurred.

config.objective: Decide if the processes in execution-leads represent unauthorized payload delivery, arch-specific binary execution, or dangerous container persistence.
config.description: Determine if the observed process activity warrants a deeper investigation into network and file-system activity.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict on whether the command-line activity is suspicious enough to open the gate.
config.success_criteria: A clear verdict for every host found in the lead query.

config.question: the evaluate-leads verdict is suspicious or malicious for at least one host
config.condition: the evaluate-leads verdict is suspicious or malicious for at least one host
config.description: Route to detailed evidence collection if the lead is suspicious, or close out early to save cost.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, process_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) as host_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (dst_endpoint_port IN (21, 69) OR (dst_endpoint_port IN (80, 443) AND (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%curl%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%wget%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%fetch%'))) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, process_name HAVING host_count <= 3
config.description: Corroborate staging leads with rare outbound connections on FTP, TFTP, or HTTP from fetch-related binaries.
config.expected_signal: Connections to external IPs on unusual staging ports or from utilities used by the fetch payloads. Rare destinations indicate targeted staging infrastructure.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, process_name, actor_user_name, activity_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (activity_id IN (1, 3, 5)) AND (file_path LIKE '/bin/%' OR file_path LIKE '/usr/bin/%' OR file_path LIKE '/sbin/%' OR file_path LIKE '/usr/sbin/%' OR instr(',' || '{{suspicious_paths}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(file_path) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify modification of core Linux binaries or new files in suspicious staging paths consistent with ELF injection.
config.expected_signal: File updates or creations in system binary paths or designated staging directories. Silence means no direct disk modification occurred in these paths.

config.objective: Determine if the combined evidence confirms a persistent foothold established via binary injection, fetch payloads, or Docker container abuse.

config.expected_signal: A final verdict citing the specific staging, networking, and file activity observed.
config.success_criteria: A malicious | suspicious | benign verdict per host with supporting row citations.

config.question: the triage-persistence verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.condition: the triage-persistence verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.description: Direct the hunt toward containment or manual analyst review.

config.instructions: Isolate the host and initiate collection of modified ELF binaries or Docker container configuration files for forensic analysis.

config.description: Confirm the automated findings and assess the extent of the intrusion.
config.instructions: Review the cited rows from all stages. For Linux binary modifications, check package manager integrity (rpm -V or debsums). For Docker containers, inspect the mount configuration and check for root access to the host.
